```{=html}
  <p class="tp-foot"><sup>*</sup>STARD-IONM is an IONM-specific extension of the STARD 2015 reporting guideline. Abbreviations used in the commentary: ND, no deterioration; PR, partial recovery; RD, reversible deterioration; ID, irreversible deterioration; Se, sensitivity; Sp, specificity; PPV/NPV, positive/negative predictive value; AUC, area under the ROC curve; NMB, neuromuscular blockade; MAP, mean arterial pressure.</p>
  <p class="tp-cite">Citation: Thirumala et al, Clin Neurophysiol 2026; 191: 2112364. doi: <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinph.2026.2112364" target="_blank" rel="noopener">10.1016/j.clinph.2026.2112364</a>.</p>

Alternatives to simple exclusion exist, such as data imputation (e.g. complete with the population mean, assign an existing value, etc.), which can be used to retain information from patients with incomplete data and reduce potential bias.\nThe methods used to deal with missing data should be stated explicitly in the text, or at the very least in the limitations of the study."

    "Report the distribution of severity of the target condition, including degree, duration, and permanence of postoperative neurologic deficit where applicable.\nIn studies using intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM) to detect or predict postoperative neurological deficits, the target condition can vary in severity—from mild, transient changes to severe, permanent impairments. Reporting this distribution is essential because the sensitivity of IONM may be higher in more severe cases, where signal changes are more pronounced. Specify the timing of baseline acquisition, the last IONM recording relative to closure, and the timing of anesthetic, physiologic, or surgical interventions after alerts.\nIn IONM studies, the index test—typically a neurophysiological alert during surgery—is often compared to a reference standard such as a postoperative neurological exam or longer-term follow-up. It is essential to report the time interval between the index test and the outcome assessment, as changes in the patient’s condition may occur due to natural recovery, delayed injury, or interventions performed after the alert. These changes can bias the relationship between the index test and the reference standard, particularly if IONM alerts lead to immediate surgical or anesthetic maneuvers that prevent a deficit from manifesting.\nTherefore, studies should describe not only the timing of follow-up (e.g., immediate post-op, discharge, or 3-month visit), but also any interventions performed in response to IONM alerts, such as stopping dissection, increasing blood pressure, or administering steroids. These actions may influence the outcome and can obscure whether the index test truly predicted the deficit or contributed to its avoidance.\nSome have proposed using the immediate intraoperative resolution of an IONM alert as an alternative or secondary reference standard, which may provide a closer temporal link and reduce post-surgical bias. Regardless of the model used, transparent reporting of both the follow-up interval and all relevant clinical interventions is critical to interpret the true diagnostic value of IONM.     "24",
    "Estimates of diagnostic accuracy and their precision (such as 95% confidence intervals), including how RD and PR were handled",
    "Report estimates of diagnostic accuracy with measures of precision (for example, 95% confidence intervals), and state how RD and PR were handled in the calculations. If sensitivity analyses were performed to show the impact of alternate classifications, report them.\nDiagnostic accuracy studies should present quantitative estimates—such as sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and odds ratios—along with measures of statistical precision, including 95% confidence intervals. P-values may be included where appropriate, though effect size and precision are more informative. These statistics enable critical appraisal of the reliability and clinical significance of the IONM modality under study.\nIONM-specific considerations: In IONM research, where sample sizes may be limited or outcomes infrequent, it's essential to report these measures transparently. If statistical estimates are not provided, authors should clearly explain why (e.g., exploratory study, limited sample). Precision measures are particularly important given the variability in intraoperative responses and outcome definitions. State how reversible deterioration/partial recovery was handled in accuracy calculations (separate category vs collapsed to ±) and provide sensitivity analyses showing its impact on Se/Sp/PPV/NPV and AUC. Report 95% CIs and model/test used for all estimates."

Reference standard-related events may involve additional imaging, neurological testing, or interventions postoperatively. Accurate reporting of such adverse events is essential to assess the safety profile of IONM and refine monitoring protocols."

For very small samples (<12), avoid inferential statistics; instead use descriptive statistics and acknowledge limitations.\nCorrection for Multiple Testing: Indicate whether multiple testing correction was performed.   const TITLE = "STARD-IONM checklist of information to include when reporting a diagnostic accuracy study of intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring";
  const FOOT = [
    "*STARD-IONM is an IONM-specific extension of the STARD 2015 reporting guideline. Abbreviations used in the commentary: ND, no deterioration; PR, partial recovery; RD, reversible deterioration; ID, irreversible deterioration; Se, sensitivity; Sp, specificity; PPV/NPV, positive/negative predictive value; AUC, area under the ROC curve; NMB, neuromuscular blockade; MAP, mean arterial pressure.",
    "Citation: Thirumala et al, Clin Neurophysiol 2026; 191: 2112364. doi: [[10.1016/j.clinph.2026.2112364|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinph.2026.2112364]]."
  ];

  const esc = s => s.replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;");
  const paras = s => s.split("\n").map(p => `<p>${esc(p)}</p>`).join("");

  const STORE = "stard-ionm-checklist-v1";
  const tbody = document.querySelector("#tp-table tbody");
  tbody.innerHTML = ROWS.map(r => {
    if (typeof r === "string") return `<tr class="sec"><td colspan="5">${r}</td></tr>`;
    if (r[0] === "L") return `<tr class="lab"><td colspan="5">${r[1]}</td></tr>`;
    const [topic, ind, items] = r, n = items.length;
    return items.map(([code, text, comm], i) =>
      `<tr>` + (i ? "" : `<td class="topic${ind ? " ind" : ""}" rowspan="${n}">${topic}</td>`) +
      `<td class="item">${code}</td><td class="txt">${paras(text)}</td><td class="cm">${paras(comm)}</td>` +
      `<td class="pg"><input type="text" data-key="p${code}" placeholder="page no." aria-label="Page, item ${code}"></td></tr>`).join("");
  }).join("");

  const fields = () => [...document.querySelectorAll("#tp-wrap input")];
  const load = () => { try { const d = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORE) || "{}");
    fields().forEach(i => { if (d[i.dataset.key]) i.value = d[i.dataset.key]; }); } catch (e) {} };
  const save = () => { try { const d = {}; fields().forEach(i => { if (i.value) d[i.dataset.key] = i.value; });
    localStorage.setItem(STORE, JSON.stringify(d)); } catch (e) {} };
  load();
  document.getElementById("tp-wrap").addEventListener("input", save);

  // Section/label rows span all visible columns: 5 on screen, 4 in print (commentary column hidden)
  const setSpan = n => document.querySelectorAll("#tp-wrap tr.sec td, #tp-wrap tr.lab td").forEach(td => td.colSpan = n);
  window.addEventListener("beforeprint", () => setSpan(4));
  window.addEventListener("afterprint", () => setSpan(5));

  // Save as PDF via the browser print dialog (print CSS shows only the checklist)
  document.getElementById("tp-pdf").onclick = () => {
    const old = document.title;
    document.title = "STARD-IONM checklist";
    window.print();
    document.title = old;
  };

  document.getElementById("tp-reset").onclick = () => {
    if (confirm("Clear all page numbers and the manuscript title?")) { fields().forEach(i => i.value = ""); save(); }
  };

  // ---- Word (.docx) export (A4 portrait) ----------------------------------
  function buildDocx(D, ROWS, vals, title, foot, eqLogo) {
    const F = "Arial", SZ = 17, W = [1500, 500, 6966, 1500], TOTAL = W.reduce((a, b) => a + b), NC = W.length;
    const ln = { style: D.BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6, color: "000000" };
    const run = (text, o = {}) => new D.TextRun({ text, font: F, size: o.size || SZ, bold: o.bold, italics: o.italic, superScript: o.sup });
    const runs = (text, o = {}) => {
      const out = [], re = /\[\[(.*?)\|(.*?)\]\]/g; let last = 0, m;
      while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
        if (m.index > last) out.push(run(text.slice(last, m.index), o));
        out.push(new D.ExternalHyperlink({ link: m[2], children: [new D.TextRun({ text: m[1], font: F, size: o.size || SZ, color: "0563C1", underline: {} })] }));
        last = re.lastIndex;
      }
      if (last < text.length) out.push(run(text.slice(last), o));
      return out;
    };
    const cell = (i, text, o = {}) => new D.TableCell({
      width: { size: o.span ? TOTAL : W[i], type: D.WidthType.DXA }, columnSpan: o.span ? NC : undefined, rowSpan: o.rowSpan,
      verticalAlign: o.mid ? D.VerticalAlign.CENTER : D.VerticalAlign.TOP,
      shading: o.fill ? { type: D.ShadingType.CLEAR, fill: o.fill, color: "auto" } : undefined,
      margins: { top: 40, bottom: 40, left: o.indent || 90, right: 90 }, borders: { top: ln, bottom: ln, left: ln, right: ln },
      children: text.split("\n").map((l, k, a) => new D.Paragraph({ keepNext: o.keepNext, spacing: { after: k < a.length - 1 ? 60 : 0 },
        alignment: o.center ? D.AlignmentType.CENTER : D.AlignmentType.LEFT, children: runs(l, o) }))
    });
    const hd = { fill: "BFBFBF", bold: true, mid: true };
    const head = new D.TableRow({ tableHeader: true, cantSplit: true, children: [
      cell(0, "Section / Topic", hd), cell(1, "No", { ...hd, center: true }),
      cell(2, "STARD item description", hd), cell(3, "Reported on page no.", hd)] });
    const body = ROWS.flatMap(r => {
      if (typeof r === "string") return [new D.TableRow({ cantSplit: true, children: [cell(0, r, { span: true, fill: "B4C6E7", bold: true, keepNext: true })] })];
      if (r[0] === "L") return [new D.TableRow({ cantSplit: true, children: [cell(0, r[1], { span: true, bold: true, italic: true, keepNext: true })] })];
      const [topic, ind, items] = r;
      return items.map(([code, text], i) => new D.TableRow({ cantSplit: false, children: [
        ...(i ? [] : [cell(0, topic, { rowSpan: items.length, indent: ind ? 260 : 90 })]),
        cell(1, code, { center: true }), cell(2, text), cell(3, vals["p" + code] || "", { center: true, mid: true })] }));
    });
    const para = (children, o = {}) => new D.Paragraph({ spacing: { after: 80 }, ...o, children });
    const footer = new D.Footer({ children: [new D.Paragraph({ alignment: D.AlignmentType.CENTER,
      children: [new D.TextRun({ children: ["Page ", D.PageNumber.CURRENT, " of ", D.PageNumber.TOTAL_PAGES], font: F, size: 18 })] })] });
    const top = [
      ...(eqLogo ? [para([new D.ImageRun({ data: eqLogo, type: "png", transformation: { width: 140, height: Math.round(140 * 90 / 310) } })],
        { alignment: D.AlignmentType.RIGHT, spacing: { after: 60 } })] : []),
      para([run(title, { bold: true, size: 24 }), run("*", { bold: true, size: 24, sup: true })], { spacing: { after: 100 } }),
      para([run("Manuscript title: ", { bold: true, size: 20 }), run(vals.title || "", { size: 20 })], { spacing: { after: 120 } })
    ];
    return new D.Document({
      title: "STARD-IONM checklist", creator: "STARD-IONM checklist",
      sections: [{
        footers: { default: footer },
        properties: { page: { size: { width: 11906, height: 16838, orientation: D.PageOrientation.PORTRAIT }, margin: { top: 720, bottom: 800, left: 720, right: 720 } } },
        children: [...top, new D.Table({ width: { size: TOTAL, type: D.WidthType.DXA }, columnWidths: W, rows: [head, ...body] }),
          ...foot.map((t, i) => para(runs(t, { size: 16 }), { spacing: { before: i ? 60 : 140 } }))]
      }]
    });
  }

  const loadDocx = () => window.docx ? Promise.resolve() : new Promise((res, rej) => {
    const el = document.createElement("script");
    el.src = new URL("docx.min.js", document.baseURI).href;
    el.onload = res; el.onerror = () => rej(new Error("Could not load docx.min.js"));
    document.head.appendChild(el);
  });

  document.getElementById("tp-doc").onclick = async () => {
    const btn = document.getElementById("tp-doc"), label = btn.textContent;
    btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = "Preparing…";
    try {
      await loadDocx();
      let eqLogo = null;
      try { eqLogo = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch(new URL("/assets/logos/equator_logo.png", document.baseURI))).arrayBuffer()); } catch (e) {}
      const vals = {}; fields().forEach(i => vals[i.dataset.key] = i.value);
      const blob = await window.docx.Packer.toBlob(buildDocx(window.docx, ROWS, vals, TITLE, FOOT, eqLogo));
      const a = document.createElement("a");
      a.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([blob], { type: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" }));
      a.download = "STARD-IONM-checklist.docx";
      document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove();
      setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href), 2000);
    } catch (e) {
      alert("Sorry, the Word file could not be created. " + e.message);
    } finally { btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = label; }
  };
})();
</script>
```
